From b31ff3cdf540110da4572e3e29bd172087af65cc Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Richard Wareing <rwareing@fb.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2017 09:09:35 +1000
Subject: [PATCH] xfs: XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE() should be false if no rt device
 present

If using a kernel with CONFIG_XFS_RT=y and we set the RHINHERIT flag on
a directory in a filesystem that does not have a realtime device and
create a new file in that directory, it gets marked as a real time file.
When data is written and a fsync is issued, the filesystem attempts to
flush a non-existent rt device during the fsync process.

This results in a crash dereferencing a null buftarg pointer in
xfs_blkdev_issue_flush():

  BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000008
  IP: xfs_blkdev_issue_flush+0xd/0x20
  .....
  Call Trace:
    xfs_file_fsync+0x188/0x1c0
    vfs_fsync_range+0x3b/0xa0
    do_fsync+0x3d/0x70
    SyS_fsync+0x10/0x20
    do_syscall_64+0x4d/0xb0
    entry_SYSCALL64_slow_path+0x25/0x25

Setting RT inode flags does not require special privileges so any
unprivileged user can cause this oops to occur.  To reproduce, confirm
kernel is compiled with CONFIG_XFS_RT=y and run:

  # mkfs.xfs -f /dev/pmem0
  # mount /dev/pmem0 /mnt/test
  # mkdir /mnt/test/foo
  # xfs_io -c 'chattr +t' /mnt/test/foo
  # xfs_io -f -c 'pwrite 0 5m' -c fsync /mnt/test/foo/bar

Or just run xfstests with MKFS_OPTIONS="-d rtinherit=1" and wait.

Kernels built with CONFIG_XFS_RT=n are not exposed to this bug.

Fixes: f538d4da8d52 ("[XFS] write barrier support")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Richard Wareing <rwareing@fb.com>
Signed-off-by: Dave Chinner <david@fromorbit.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/fs/xfs/xfs_linux.h b/fs/xfs/xfs_linux.h
index 9301c5a6060b..dcd1292664b3 100644
--- a/fs/xfs/xfs_linux.h
+++ b/fs/xfs/xfs_linux.h
@@ -270,7 +270,14 @@ static inline uint64_t howmany_64(uint64_t x, uint32_t y)
 #endif /* DEBUG */
 
 #ifdef CONFIG_XFS_RT
-#define XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE(ip) ((ip)->i_d.di_flags & XFS_DIFLAG_REALTIME)
+
+/*
+ * make sure we ignore the inode flag if the filesystem doesn't have a
+ * configured realtime device.
+ */
+#define XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE(ip)			\
+	(((ip)->i_d.di_flags & XFS_DIFLAG_REALTIME) &&	\
+	 (ip)->i_mount->m_rtdev_targp)
 #else
 #define XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE(ip) (0)
 #endif
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `fs/xfs/xfs_linux.h`**
   - The macro `XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE(ip)` has been modified. 
   - The new definition checks two conditions:
     - Whether the inode's flags indicate it is a real-time inode (`(ip)->i_d.di_flags & XFS_DIFLAG_REALTIME`).
     - Whether the filesystem has a configured real-time device (`(ip)->i_mount->m_rtdev_targp`).
   - If either condition is false, the macro will return false, preventing the marking of an inode as a real-time inode when no real-time device is present.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `xfs_linux.h` directly addresses the bug described in the patch. By ensuring that the inode is only considered a real-time inode if a real-time device is configured, the patch prevents the kernel from attempting to flush a non-existent real-time device during file operations, which was causing a crash due to dereferencing a null pointer. This change is crucial for maintaining system stability when using the XFS filesystem with real-time features enabled.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs when a directory is marked with the RHINHERIT flag in a filesystem that does not have a configured real-time device. This leads to newly created files being incorrectly marked as real-time files. When an fsync operation is performed on these files, the filesystem attempts to flush a non-existent real-time device, resulting in a kernel crash due to dereferencing a null pointer.

Here is the patch:
 
 #ifdef CONFIG_XFS_RT
-#define XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE(ip) ((ip)->i_d.di_flags & XFS_DIFLAG_REALTIME)
+
+/*
+ * make sure we ignore the inode flag if the filesystem doesn't have a
+ * configured realtime device.
+ */

+	 (ip)->i_mount->m_rtdev_targp)
 #else
 #define XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE(ip) (0)

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE(ip) ((ip)->i_d.di_flags & XFS_DIFLAG_REALTIME)
```
```c
(ip)->i_mount->m_rtdev_targp
```
Reason:
The first statement checks if an inode is marked as a real-time inode based on its flags. If a directory is marked with the RHINHERIT flag in a filesystem without a real-time device, newly created files are incorrectly marked as real-time. The second statement attempts to access the real-time device target pointer during an fsync operation, leading to a null pointer dereference when the device does not exist, causing a kernel crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE(ip)			\
	(((ip)->i_d.di_flags & XFS_DIFLAG_REALTIME) &&	\
	 (ip)->i_mount->m_rtdev_targp)
```
Reason:
This modified definition of `XFS_IS_REALTIME_INODE` adds a check to ensure that the inode is only considered a real-time inode if the filesystem has a configured real-time device (`m_rtdev_targp`). This prevents the kernel from attempting to flush a non-existent real-time device, thus avoiding the null pointer dereference and subsequent crash.
